es: Crear una metáfora, un símil y una personificación propios sobre un lugar o una estación, evitar los tópicos y explicar por qué cada imagen funciona en un texto breve y coherente.

vocabulary.es: un toque de, una pizca de

teaching.en: Autumn is a golden painter: within a few weeks it changes every tree in the park, and the whole street looks newly coloured.
teaching.es: El otoño es un pintor dorado: en pocas semanas cambia todos los árboles del parque y la calle entera parece recién coloreada.
teaching.explanationEs: Metáfora original: Autumn is a…; el resto de la frase desarrolla la imagen del pintor.
segments: Autumn is a golden painter: within a few weeks it changes every
tree in the park, and the whole street looks newly coloured.
teaching.audioText: Autumn is a golden painter: within a few weeks it changes every tree in the park, and the whole street looks newly coloured.

teaching.en: The fallen leaves lie on the path like a carpet, and they rustle softly whenever somebody walks across them.
teaching.es: Las hojas caídas yacen en el camino como una alfombra, y crujen suavemente cada vez que alguien pasa por encima.
teaching.explanationEs: Símil: like + nombre. Rustle es el sonido de hojas secas o de papel; es más preciso que «make a noise».
segments: The fallen leaves lie on the path like a carpet,
and they rustle softly whenever somebody walks across them.
teaching.audioText: The fallen leaves lie on the path like a carpet, and they rustle softly whenever somebody walks across them.

teaching.en: In the evening the leaves seem to dance in the wind, and then they fall silent as the air becomes still.
teaching.es: Por la tarde las hojas parecen bailar con el viento, y luego se quedan en silencio cuando el aire se queda quieto.
teaching.explanationEs: Personificación: las hojas hacen algo humano, bailar. Fall silent = quedarse callado de repente.
segments: In the evening the leaves seem to dance in the wind,
and then they fall silent as the air becomes still.
teaching.audioText: In the evening the leaves seem to dance in the wind, and then they fall silent as the air becomes still.

teaching.en: I like this season because the air is cool, and when I breathe slowly I can enjoy the smell of the wet leaves.
teaching.es: Me gusta esta estación porque el aire es fresco, y cuando respiro despacio puedo disfrutar del olor de las hojas mojadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Because + motivo te sirve para explicar por qué te gusta algo o por qué funciona tu imagen.
segments: I like this season because the air is cool, and when I
breathe slowly I can enjoy the smell of the wet leaves.
teaching.audioText: I like this season because the air is cool, and when I breathe slowly I can enjoy the smell of the wet leaves.

teaching.en: I chose the word carpet because it shows how thick and soft the leaves are, whereas a cliché such as gold coins would sound tired.
teaching.es: Elegí la palabra alfombra porque muestra lo espesas y suaves que son las hojas, mientras que un tópico como monedas de oro sonaría gastado.
teaching.explanationEs: I chose… because… justifica la imagen; compararla con un tópico muestra por qué la tuya es mejor.
segments: I chose the word carpet because it shows how thick and soft the
leaves are, whereas a cliché such as gold coins would sound tired.
teaching.audioText: I chose the word carpet because it shows how thick and soft the leaves are, whereas a cliché such as gold coins would sound tired.

teaching.en: A good writer, like a painter, makes each image stand out by avoiding expressions that everybody uses and adding a hint of surprise.
teaching.es: Un buen escritor, como un pintor, hace que cada imagen destaque evitando las expresiones que todo el mundo usa y añadiendo un toque de sorpresa.
teaching.explanationEs: Stand out = destacar; a hint of + nombre = una pizca de algo.
segments: A good writer, like a painter, makes each image stand out by
avoiding expressions that everybody uses and adding a hint of surprise.
teaching.audioText: A good writer, like a painter, makes each image stand out by avoiding expressions that everybody uses and adding a hint of surprise.

prompt.es: Elige la tercera línea que añade personificación sin mezclar imágenes.

choices.text: At dusk the trees whisper to the wind and then fall silent.
The wind is as cold as ice and as loud as a train.
Autumn is also a dark prison where the trees wait to be free.

feedback.es: Solo la línea de los árboles que susurran da acciones humanas a cosas y sigue en la misma escena; las otras usan un símil o cambian de imagen.

hint.es: Busca la frase en que algo no humano hace algo humano, sin entrar en un campo nuevo.

origin.text: Mia's draft: 'Autumn is a golden painter. The leaves lie like a carpet along the path.' She now needs a third line that adds personification and keeps the same autumn scene.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hay un toque de tristeza en el último verso.»

feedback.es: A hint of + nombre es la colocación para un matiz muy leve: aquí, un toque de tristeza en un poema alegre.

hint.es: Es la palabra de la enseñanza que significa «una pizca de»: a ___ of…

origin.text: The text describes a happy summer evening, but there is a ___ of sadness in the last line, as if the writer already knew that the season was ending.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Elegí el pintor porque muestra cómo el otoño cambia los árboles.»

answer.text: I chose the painter because it shows how autumn changes the trees

feedback.es: I chose… because it shows… justifica la imagen: el sujeto it es obligatorio delante de shows.

hint.es: Empieza con I chose the painter y termina con the trees.

prompt.es: Escucha a la alumna y elige por qué eligió la imagen de los perros.

choices.text: Because the children really had dogs in the snow.
Because the image shows how playful the children are.
Because her teacher had suggested that comparison.

feedback.es: La alumna justifica la imagen con la forma de jugar de los perros, que coincide con el comportamiento de los niños; no hubo perros reales ni sugerencia.

origin.audio: I read my text to the class. I wrote that winter is a white blanket and that the children are little dogs running through it. My teacher smiled and asked why I had chosen the dogs. I told her that dogs never walk in the snow; they jump and play and run in circles, and that is exactly how the children act.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada descripción de paisaje con su tipo de imagen.

pairs: The lake is a silver mirror under the hills.
The path is as quiet as an empty church.
The trees breathe slowly in the cold night.
The bus to the village leaves at six.

feedback.es: El espejo es una metáfora, as…as marca un símil, los árboles que respiran son personificación y el autobús es un dato literal.

pairs: The lake is a silver mirror under the hills.
The path is as quiet as an empty church.
The trees breathe slowly in the cold night.
The bus to the village leaves at six.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuando el viento sopla, las hojas secas crujen suavemente.»

feedback.es: Rustle es el verbo preciso para el sonido suave de hojas secas, y además las hace «hablar» entre sí.

origin.text: When the wind blows through the park, the dry leaves ___ softly, as if they were telling secrets to each other before the night arrives.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le pide la profesora al estudiante en su comentario?

choices.text: To keep the simile but replace the animal metaphor.
To turn the personification into a simile about snow.
To replace the tired simile with one that fits the animal.

feedback.es: La profesora elogia la metáfora y la personificación y solo objeta el símil tópico, que tampoco encaja con el animal.

origin.text: Teacher's comment: 'Your first image, the sea is a blue animal, is fresh. The whisper in the evening works well too. But as white as snow is a cliché, and it does not match the animal, so please change it.'

prompt.es: Escucha a la alumna y elige qué actitud muestra ante la crítica.

choices.text: She accepts part of it but defends her choice.
She rejects it completely and will not change anything.
She agrees entirely and regrets using the image.

feedback.es: Dice «I disagree a little» y defiende que la imagen encaja con la calma buscada, pero admite que la próxima vez buscará algo más llamativo.

origin.audio: For my description of the city at night I wrote that the streets sleep and the lights are tiny moons. Some classmates said that these images are a cliché. I disagree a little: the image is old, but it matches the quiet that I wanted. Still, next time I will look for something that stands out more.

prompt.es: Completa: «En un poema breve cada imagen debe destacar.»

feedback.es: Stand out es el verbo con partícula que significa destacar: sin out la frase pierde su sentido.

origin.text: In a short text, every image has to stand ___, so avoid the expressions that everybody has already heard a thousand times and look for one that surprises the reader.

prompt.es: Describe un mercado lluvioso con metáfora, símil, personificación y explicación.

answer.text: On a rainy Saturday the market was a grey river. People moved between the stalls like leaves on the water, and the rain danced on the roofs and whispered to the fruit. The lamps were golden apples in the dark morning, and the whole place seemed to breathe warm air. I chose the river because it shows how the crowd never stops moving, even when the weather is bad. The sellers called their prices, and the smell of bread and coffee made everybody smile. A hint of sadness hung over the umbrellas, yet the noise was so cheerful that I forgot the cold. It was a noisy, colourful place, and I felt small in the middle of it, like a boat on the river.
accepted: On a rainy Saturday the market was a grey river. People moved between the stalls like leaves on the water, and the rain danced on the roofs and whispered to the fruit. The lamps were golden apples in the dark morning, and the whole place seemed to breathe warm air. I chose the river because it shows how the crowd never stops moving, even when the weather is bad. The sellers called their prices, and the smell of bread and coffee made everybody smile. A hint of sadness hung over the umbrellas, yet the noise was so cheerful that I forgot the cold. It was a noisy, colourful place, and I felt small in the middle of it, like a boat on the river.

Yesterday the market was a big kitchen on a rainy day. The sellers shouted like cooks, and the crowd moved as slowly as a river between the stalls. The rain danced on the umbrellas and sang a quiet song. The fruit looked like small lamps, red and yellow and green, and the smell of bread and coffee was a warm hug for everybody. I chose the kitchen because it shows how warm and busy the place was, even when the sky was grey. Everybody was wet, but everybody was smiling, and the market kept breathing until the evening. A hint of sugar and smoke stayed in my clothes when I finally walked home, and I did not mind at all.

feedback.es: Un buen texto mantiene una sola escena, combina las tres figuras y cierra con una frase que explica por qué funciona una de ellas.

origin.text: Describe un mercado en un día de lluvia. Escribe unas 130 palabras (mínimo 112) con una metáfora, un símil y una personificación que formen una sola escena, y explica en una frase por qué elegiste una de las imágenes.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la crítica principal de esta reseña del poema?

choices.text: The writer uses too many similes instead of metaphors.
The images are attractive but do not form one picture.
The painter image is too common to surprise the reader.

feedback.es: La reseña califica cada imagen de bonita, pero las sitúa en «three different places»: el problema es la falta de coherencia.

origin.text: Review: 'The writer calls autumn a painter, the leaves a carpet and the wind a dancer. Each image is pretty, but together they belong to three different places. The text would be stronger with only the painter, who could then mix the red, colour the trees and wait for the night to cover the work.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Elegí la palabra «espejo» porque muestra lo quieto que está el lago.»

feedback.es: I chose… because… es la fórmula para justificar una imagen; se usa el pasado chose, no el infinitivo choose.

origin.text: I ___ the word mirror because it shows how still the lake is, although a different writer might have preferred glass or silver for the same scene.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige por qué resulta vívida la descripción del hermano.

choices.text: Because he used many different kinds of figures.
Because he described every old house in great detail.
Because all the images belong to a single scene.

feedback.es: La hablante explica que todas las imágenes forman una sola escena; no cita la variedad de figuras ni el detalle de cada casa.

origin.audio: My brother described our old street in autumn. He said the houses were tired old men and the leaves were a golden carpet for their feet. I laughed, but I noticed that he had built one single picture, with old men and a carpet and feet, and that is why his description felt so vivid.
